name: Ceftolozane-tazobactam
executiveSummary: Anti-Pseudomonas cephalosporin + inhibitor. Adult cIAI/cUTI **1.5 g IV every 8 h**; HABP/VAP **3 g every 8 h**. Pediatrics **~30 mg/kg every 8 h** of product (max **1.5 g**); severe up to **45 mg/kg**.
indications:
## Indications

- Complicated intra-abdominal infection (cIAI), complicated UTI / pyelonephritis.
- Hospital-acquired / ventilator-associated pneumonia (HABP/VAP) — high dose.
- Reserved for MDR Pseudomonas / failure of other options.

## Precautions

- Mandatory renal adjustment. Each vial ~230 mg Na+.
- In cIAI often combined with metronidazole if extra anaerobes needed.

> Doses refer to **total ceftolozane + tazobactam** (1 g + 0.5 g = 1.5 g).

adulto.dose: cIAI / cUTI / pyelonephritis: **1.5 g IV every 8 h**. HABP/VAP: **3 g IV every 8 h**. Adjust by CrCl per label.
adulto.administration: Reconstitute 10 mL SW/NS; dilute in 100 mL NS/D5W; infuse **60 min**.

pediatrico.dose: **30 mg/kg every 8 h** of combined product (max **1.5 g**/dose). Severe infection: up to **45 mg/kg every 8 h** (per label; adults VAP use 3 g).

stability:
## Stability

- Reconstituted: ~1 h room temp.
- Diluted: ~24 h room temp or up to ~7 days refrigerated (label).
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Nausea, diarrhea, headache, fever, hypokalemia, ↑ transaminases, *C. difficile*, infusion-site reactions.
